deep.reconstruction:
Context: 1835 observations in the Göttingen magnetic observatory. The previous page is headed 'effect of frictional electricity on the bar'. The readings are mirror-scale divisions of a suspended magnetometer bar.

PART A (top, continuation of the previous page). These are readings r(t) taken every 10 s, from 9h43'0.5'' to 9h45'40.5''. The bar oscillates with a period of about 40 s, so readings 20 s apart are in opposite phase.
- Column 2 (verified for every line; the formula is my identification): it is the symmetric mean of the two neighbouring readings, m(t) = [r(t-10s) + r(t+10s)]/2.
  - Examples: 43'10'': (662.4+655.8)/2 = 659.1. 43'20'': (656.0+662.3)/2 = 659.15. 44'0'': (674.5+665.8)/2 = 670.15.
  - The first value, 43'0.5'' -> 659.6, uses the last reading on the previous page: (663.2+656.0)/2.
  - Averaging two readings half a period apart cancels the oscillation and leaves the momentary rest position.
- Column 3: averages of m over the plateaus where the rest position is steady.
  - 659.125 = mean(659.1, 659.15).
  - 669.800 = mean(670.05, 670.15, 669.2).
  - 659.033 = mean(659.15, 659.0, 658.95).
  - 669.025 = mean(668.9, 669.15).
- The rest position alternates between about 659 and about 669. So the electrical action shifts the bar by about 10 divisions, and the state is reversed roughly every 43 s.
- Right margin (my reading): the times listed there (32'49.2'' ... 44'20.7'') are spaced about 43.1 s apart; 37'8.0'' to 38'35.6'' is a double step, marked by a dash. These are the reversal or reading epochs used on the next page, which tabulates the differences of about 10.0-11.0 divisions.

PART B (Oct. 25, 1835). Three sets of large-amplitude turning-point readings.
- (1) Set at 10h2'14.7''.
  - Turning points: 102.3, 586.8, 103.1, 584.8.
  - Pairwise means of successive turning points: 344.55, 344.95, 343.95.
  - Mean a = 344.483 (written 344.48).
- (2) Set at 10h5'50.5''.
  - Turning points: 1187.0, 830.7, 1186.3, 831.3, 1186.0.
  - Pairwise means: 1008.85, 1008.5, 1008.8, 1008.65.
  - Mean b = 1008.7.
- (3) Set at 10h9'51.5''.
  - Turning points: 100.8, 577.1, 101.9, 575.8, 104.1, 575.7, 106.2, 574.8.
  - Pairwise means: 338.95, 339.5, 338.85, 339.95, 339.9, 340.95, 340.5.
  - Mean c = 339.8.
- Sets 1 and 3 are one deflected position and set 2 is the opposite one. This is a deflection experiment of Gauss's Intensitas type, with the deflector reversed. The arrangement a-b-c in time is symmetric, so linear drift cancels.
- The combination:
  - a+b = 1353.183 (written, then struck out).
  - b+c = 1348.500.
  - Sum 2701.683; divided by 4 gives 675.421 = (a+2b+c)/4. This is the undeflected (mean) position.
  - b-a = 664.217 and b-c = 668.900; sum 1333.117.
  - 1333.117/4 = 333.279 = [b-(a+c)/2]/2. This is the half-difference, i.e. the deflection, labelled 'M.O' (magnetisches Observatorium).
- Beside it, 'Stern 351.362' is presumably the corresponding deflection obtained at the Sternwarte, for comparing the horizontal intensity (or the instrumental constants) at the two sites. Ratio 351.362/333.279 ≈ 1.0543; this is my computation and is not on the page.
errors: No arithmetic errors found. Every pairwise mean, plateau mean and the final combination check.
Minor: 344.483 is written as 344.48 in the box, but the full value 344.483 is used later (1353.183, 664.217), so this is consistent.
The struck-out 1353.183 (= a+b) is not an error. It is simply replaced by recording b+c = 1348.500 and the total 2701.683.

results.what: Rest position of an oscillating magnetometer as the mean of readings half a period apart (successive turning points), then averaged over plateaus
results.modern_name: Elimination of free oscillation by averaging opposite-phase readings (rest-point determination)

results.what: Symmetric combination (a+2b+c)/4 for the mean position and [b-(a+c)/2]/2 for the deflection, eliminating linear drift
results.modern_name: Symmetric (time-centred) observing scheme / drift elimination in a deflection experiment

results.what: Measurement of the ~10-division deflection of the magnetometer under alternating action of frictional electricity
